sections.title: Player read-aloud
sections.body: A vendor cart lies sideways across the road. Produce and invoices spill into the mud. A polished placard blinks: INCIDENT RESPONSE EXPECTED WITHIN 3–5 BUSINESS DAYS.

sections.title: Scene summary
sections.body: The party finds a vendor cart blocking the road, with spilled produce, invoices, and a useless incident placard.

sections.title: Visible choices
items: Investigate the cart
Move the cart
Call out into the woods
Approach the body

sections.title: Player questions
items: What detail in The Overturned Vendor Cart tells you the official story is incomplete?
Who notices the human cost first, and how do they show it?
What small object, smell, or sound makes this scene feel real?
What cheerful warning sign did your character dismiss as marketing copy before realizing it was true?

sections.title: GM notes
items: The placard can be a standard route-monitoring glyph, not proof that anyone meaningfully knows what happened.
Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it.
Sablewood route lore: this is an approved path, and the body/cart disruption should feel like a coverage failure as much as a wilderness event.
Manufactured-threat lens: seed the contradiction, do not explain it. The surface goal stays simple and heroic.
[KEEP/EARNED] The driver died from a cut throat; the strixwolf did not kill him. (Instinct or Knowledge Medium 15)
[ADD/EARNED] Near the cart is a pre-written Grail "Hazard Confirmed: Strixwolf Attack" tag. (Finesse or Instinct Medium 15)

sections.title: Checks and rolls
items: Instinct or Knowledge Separate animal scavenging from staged violence. Standard The PCs learn Tamsin was likely killed by humanoids. 15 Cleanly resolve: Separate animal scavenging from staged violence. Add a concrete boon, extra clue, or improved position. Success, plus the player names one helpful detail or asks one follow-up question. Success, but the GM exposes a cost, ticks a countdown, or reveals a new pressure tied to The Overturned Vendor Cart. The full goal slips, but the party still learns a useful truth or avoids the worst consequence. The GM makes a hard move that follows from the fiction and leaves the next choice visible. Spend Fear to separate true evidence from a tempting false read, or put the carriage/cargo under time pressure. On mixed or sliding results, reveal information in layers: visible fact, actionable clue, then systemic truth.

sections.title: Clues
items: Route Ledger The delivery was delayed. Someone manipulated the logistics trail. The ledger's time marks do not match the official route.
Bramble Strand Someone else was here. Bramble Union scouts marked the site. A tied plant-fiber marker under the cart.

sections.title: Loot
items: Use Vendor Cart and Tamsin Vell search tables

Keystone Asset™: Inside the sealed crate, packed in wax-paper and reassurance, sits a heavy grey stone the size of a loaf, warm to the touch, faintly humming, with a light deep inside it that is slowly going out.

Incident Response Placard™: A flat brass disc on a post holds a watchful glyph and a single cheerful bell. When trouble happens nearby, the glyph lights, the bell rings once, brightly, and then nothing else happens at all.

Sableblade: Growing straight up out of dark forest soil, like a sapling that decided to be a sword, is a blade of living dark wood and pale metal. It has no maker's mark and hums when your hand nears the hilt.
Recall Stone: A smooth grey pebble feels warm and ordinary until it refuses to stay where you put it. Set it down, look away, and it waits back in your palm.
Goldwater Liability Token™: A heavy brass chit with a smiling coin-face drops into your palm like a tiny verdict. The fine print is too small to read without feeling blamed.
Tamsin's Home-Token: A small thumb-polished token on a cord hangs beside the torn blue scarf, warm from wear and etched with a tiny house mark instead of a company seal.
Cracked Pocket Ward™: A cheap little ward charm sits cracked down the middle, still trying to glow through a smiling warranty sticker.

sections.title: Mechanics
items: Plot So Far: The party is in Act One pressure: The party finds a vendor cart blocking the road, with spilled produce, invoices, and a useless incident placard.

Mechanics In Play: Use Daggerheart Duality Dice as baseline. Use the listed Difficulty and outcome options when a roll matters. Keep trivial actions no-roll; roll only when uncertainty, cost, or danger is interesting.

Roll Cards: s01-02-search-tamsin-vell S01-02 Search Tamsin Vell Search Tamsin Vell Instinct Knowledge Instinct Knowledge 12 Instinct notices wounds and threat posture; Knowledge reconstructs the scene. A false monster-read hides the murder. Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction. Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous. Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure. Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option. Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction. A false monster-read hides the murder. Use a hard complication, lost time...
Gm Fear Spends: Make the safe road feel less safe: noise, scent, cracked wheel, or cargo hum. Separate evidence from assumption so a monster read is tempting but incomplete.
Conditions Hazards: Hidden
Search Loot Clues: Search Tamsin Vell / Vendor Cart: Pocket Ward, manifest, Goldwater slip, route ledger, lived-in details.
No Roll Guidance: Do not call for a roll when the players have time, a clear method, and no meaningful pressure.
Escalation: Escalate by making cost visible: time, noise, trust, ward instability, or someone vulnerable in danger.
Deescalation: De-escalate through respect, care, honest testimony, useful evidence, or a concrete concession.
Tv Mechanics Caption: Public cue: The Overturned Vendor Cart asks what the party does, what it costs, and who is protected.

Trait Variety Note: Primary traits in this scene: Finesse, Instinct, Knowledge. If rolls drift toward Instinct/Presence, ask whether Agility, Strength, Finesse, or Knowledge better describes the action.

Class Community Ancestry Reveals: Loreborne: spots older legal, heraldic, or ward-craft language under the branding. Underborne: notices service doors, hidden routes, and who built the thing nobody credits. Highborne: reads etiquette, class panic, and reputational risk. Ridgeborne: notices stonework, weight, pressure, and structural weakness. Wildborne: reads the land, animals, and local ecological stress. Elf/Ribbet/Human/Giant/Katari: invite one sensory or social detail from the player's heritage. Sorcerer/Rogue/Warrior/Guardian/Ranger: give each class one table-facing way to shine without changing the plot.
